Fresh input may re-take ownership while moving only after prior verified ACTIVE in the same uninterrupted session, completed restoration, fresh valid CAN and exact firmware profile. OFF/CANCEL/hard faults/restarts do not auto-resume.
controller_startup.button_fix: Physical toggles are monitored by firmware across NO_OUTPUT/ELM/Hyundai transitions with the same I5R1 profile. First held button at cold start is not a new ON; SET initial release is inhibited until neutral. Host brake/ACC latch and firmware permission-reduction request prevent stale health re-enabling longitudinal.

input_contract.final_upstream_contract: Agreed on 2026-10-06: existing ActuationCommand.lateral is steering-wheel angle rate in deg/s, acceleration is longitudinal acceleration in m/s^2. Only these two fields are required under use_enable_field=false. Non-latched 20 Hz publication recommended; physical steering sign and actual cadence/jitter still require integration validation.

bridge_assessment.requested_architecture: Upper ROS controller -> command adapter/CAN bridge -> Panda ECAN -> lateral and longitudinal vehicle ECUs.
bridge_assessment.input_semantics_and_units: Still require the upstream contract; do not assume angle, angle-rate, torque, curvature, target speed, or acceleration are interchangeable.
bridge_assessment.longitudinal: With current scale=1/offset=0 and unfiltered_input=true, valid acceleration in m/s^2 is copied into both SCC acceleration-request fields, quantized to 0.01 m/s^2, without host jerk slew. carrotpilot_comparison.scope: Read-only source research of the current default branch snapshot; no runtime-pin, control-code, firmware, or vehicle changes.
model_to_can: modeld publishes modelV2.action desiredCurvature, desiredAcceleration, desiredVelocity, and shouldStop; targets may be derived from the predicted plan or a model action head.
Lateral path selects model action or lane-based lateralPlan, applies smoothing/curvature limiting, and uses a feedback controller to compute torque or angle according to vehicle configuration.
Longitudinal planner combines model trajectory/action, radar and cruise/MPC targets. ACC mode uses MPC; the other path takes the lower model/MPC acceleration and velocity targets.
LongControl combines target feedforward with measured speed or acceleration feedback, stop/start states and acceleration limits; controlsd publishes carControl at 100 Hz.

card calls CarInterface.apply, Hyundai CarController applies platform-specific conversion and limits, and the CAN packer constructs frames. sendcan passes through native pandad to Panda and vehicle CAN.
CAN-FD torque steering uses LFA TORQUE_REQUEST (the corresponding local pinned DBC signal is StrTqReqVal); SCC_CONTROL carries aReqRaw and aReqValue, with additional jerk shaping of aReqValue.
carrotpilot_comparison.feedback: carOutput.actuatorsOutput reports software CarController outputs. The requested-versus-returned steering comparison detects controller limiting; it is not ECU acknowledgement or physical torque measurement. CAN-FD CarState separately decodes MDPS steering/output torque and fault bits.
carrotpilot_comparison.angle_control: Current upstream includes ANGLE_CONTROL/LFA_ALT detection and LKAS_ANGLE_CMD plus an authority ceiling. This does not establish native angle-command support on this project vehicle (2022 Ioniq 5 HDA1); local output remains torque.

recovery.temporary_steering_fault: Temporary MDPS fault blocks latActive. The general SOFT_DISABLE state has a 3-second timer; disappearance of soft-disable conditions before expiry returns to enabled. Silent temporary steering events have different alert classification.
recovery.can_loss: canTimeout becomes canBusMissing, invalid CAN becomes canError. Both events are IMMEDIATE_DISABLE and NO_ENTRY. After disabled, state-machine engagement requires a new ENABLE event with NO_ENTRY absent; signal recovery alone is not the transition.
recovery.always_lateral_caveat: This fork has AlwaysLateral and independent lateral gates. Do not equate a global disabled state with every lateral-path condition; steerFaultTemporary/Permanent directly prohibit lateral activation.
recovery.panda_transport: Native pandad exits when a Panda disconnects; its Python wrapper loops and re-enumerates/reconnects and relaunches the native process. This does not confirm ECU recovery. Native sender discards messages older than one second.
recovery.startup_ecu_session: Hyundai init calls disable_ecu for configured longitudinal ownership. disable_ecu retries initial setup up to 10 times; periodic suppressed-response tester-present maintains the diagnostic session. This is not a continuous positive ECU response check.
recovery.steering_override: recovering_from_override and SteeringHandover recover steering authority after driver intervention, especially in the angle path; these are unrelated to reconnecting an unresponsive ECU.
recovery.ecu_restore_scope: No general in-motion ECU reset or stock-camera/radar restoration-and-rearm state machine was found in the inspected Hyundai runtime path. CarInterfaceBase.deinit is a stub and Hyundai does not override it in this snapshot.
recovery.local_comparison: The local pending camera/radar communication-restoration retries, valid-stock-traffic and Panda NO_OUTPUT confirmation, and explicit rearm gating are this project implementation, not functionality established by the inspected Carrotpilot runtime path.

power_startup_assessment.boot_behavior: Pinned Panda boot initializes stock-connected harness and SILENT. No-host heartbeat fallback is SILENT/power-save, not automatic vehicle takeover. Earlier MCU boot does not prevent later safety-mode RX reset, USB startup queue handling or ECU communication-control interruption.

power_startup_assessment.conclusion: Independent Panda power is a plausible power/boot-order improvement, not a demonstrated fix for the recorded ECU faults. No comma-power comparison, power-cycle, wiring, Panda query or vehicle test performed.
